## Professional Summary

Physical scientist at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency studying what it takes to reuse water safely. Serves as a technical authority and subject matter expert on the risks and treatment of chemical and microbial contaminants in water. Uses cheminformatics to screen chemicals in oil and gas wastewater, informs federal discharge rules, and builds R tools for working with EPA chemical data.

---

## Technical Skills

| Area | Details |
|:-----|:--------|
| **Programming & Databases** | R (Shiny, Package Development), SQL, Python, Database Architecture |
| **Data Analysis, Modeling, ML/AI** | Cheminformatics, Statistical Analysis, Predictive Modeling, Machine Learning (Classification, Regression), Data Mining & Curation, Generative AI / LLMs (Text Classification, Summarization, Data Labeling) |
| **Visualization & Reporting** | R Shiny, ggplot2, Plotly, Quarto, Markdown, Data Storytelling |
| **Regulatory & Policy Expertise** | Expertise in Clean Water Act (CWA), Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), and related environmental regulations; Development and review of environmental policies, technical standards, and regulatory guidelines |
| **Water Resource & Program Management** | Technical expertise in reviewing water quality protection, restoration, and regulatory compliance for drinking water programs; Programmatic coordination with states, tribes, and stakeholders on water resource initiatives; Design, execution, and oversight of environmental studies for water quality assessment and improvement |
| **Methodologies & Practices** | Research Planning & Execution, Data Quality Assurance, Stakeholder Communication & Collaboration (oral & written), Risk Communication, Technical Documentation & Written Communication |

## Professional Experience

::: {.cv-entry}
[**Physical Scientist (series 1301), GS-12**]{.cv-title} [(40 hrs/wk)]{.cv-note} [Jan 2025 -- Present]{.cv-date}

US Environmental Protection Agency [Cincinnati, OH]{.cv-date}
:::

- Curate chemical disclosures from *FracFocus*, including where and when chemicals were used in oil and gas operations. The data support work on federal wastewater discharge rules and emergency response.
- Develop *CompToxR*, an R package that gives researchers access to EPA chemical data and tools for hazard screening, toxicity evaluation, and non-targeted analysis (screening samples for chemicals without a predefined list). The package connects researchers to EPA workflows and resources including GenRA, ECOTOX, and EPI Suite.
- Develop *THREAT* (Toxicological, Hazard, Risk Evaluation Assessment Tool), an R Shiny app that lets users upload their water sample results, compare sites and chemicals against environmental benchmarks, and prioritize follow-up.
- Advised on an emergency response using EPA research and analysis from a produced-water reuse study. Received EPA Region 8’s *Shooting Star* award for the work.
- Support EPA Office of Research and Development projects by assessing risks for specific water uses (SSWR.406.1), curating data on chemical structures, samples, and properties (CSS.407.1), and combining evidence from different fields in case studies that support chemical safety decisions (CSS.408.3).
- Currently holds a Level 4 (Moderate Risk) security clearance.

### Technical Support {.cv-subsection}

- Combined more than ten years of monitoring data from eight laboratories and led the analysis for EPA Region 8’s *Evaluation of Produced Water Intended for Beneficial Reuse in Multiple Oil and Gas Basins*. Developed an R Shiny app that uses field and experimental results to prioritize sites using EPA cheminformatics tools and assessments of acute, chronic, and cumulative toxicity. Partners included EPA Regions 3 and 6, EPA research centers, and the U.S. Department of Energy’s National Energy Technology Laboratory.

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Assess risks from chemicals known or suspected to occur in produced water, the wastewater generated during oil and gas extraction. Work with EPA’s Office of Science and Technology and regional offices to inform revisions to the Oil and Gas Extraction Effluent Guidelines, the federal discharge rules for the industry (40 CFR 435 Subpart E).

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Help develop a workflow to assess short- and long-term risks to people and ecosystems and identify potential uses for treated produced water. Previously led the New Mexico Produced Water Research Consortium’s Risk and Toxicology work group and contribute to its multistate coordination and water data efforts.

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Develop an R Shiny app that reads lead service line inventories in different state formats and produces records for field verification. The app supports federally funded technical assistance for the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (SSWR.411.3).

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Develop chemical property inputs from EPA CompTox data and a random forest model to predict how effectively different wastewater treatment technologies remove unregulated contaminants. This work supports the EPA Office of Water and its contractors through the *Integrated Performance Framework for Emerging Contaminants in Wastewater Treatment Plants*, which evaluates treatment costs and removal effectiveness.

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Provide technical support to New Mexico State University on non-targeted analysis and whole effluent toxicity testing to identify chemicals and assess acute and chronic toxicity of produced water as a mixture.

::: {.cv-thin-separator}
:::

- Serve as the chemical risk subject matter expert and data analyst, integrating microbial and chemical measurements, in vitro assays, and non-targeted analysis results into datasets partners can use. This work supports *Potable Water Reuse in Protein Production and Processing* with Tyson Foods, the University of Nebraska, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture, and EPA’s *Evaluating the Microbial and Chemical Quality of Air Handler Unit Condensate* project.
